text:
Broad Street Hockey thinks the Flyers may have underestimated Oliver Bonk's offensive ceiling. Our numbers are cautious, but they lean that way too. At 21, in effectively his rookie season, he has 6 points in 12 games and plays almost 19 minutes a night, including 24:24 against Colorado.

His goal against Utah on Nov. 1 was a slap shot past Karel Vejmelka, and at least one outlet mistook it for his first in the NHL. (It wasn't: he scored in his one game last season.) The bigger picture: Philadelphia has scored 6.2 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and the Flyers are almost six points better in expected goal share (the quality of chances) with him than without.

The comparison: of the 57 defensemen picked 17th to 27th since 2005 with four-plus seasons, the median first full season was 0.21 points a game. Bonk has 6 in 12 games. The closest picks range from K'Andre Miller to Olli Maatta. Our projection runs wide, 25 to 52 points, because the sample is small. That uncertainty is the fun part. He's the 22nd pick from 2023, and he's playing like he belongs.
headline: Oliver Bonk, a little ahead of schedule
